Subject: Your complaint - unauthorised access on 7 July 2026

Dear [Customer Name],

Thank you for your patience while we carried out a full review of your complaint.

My name is [Name], one of the Senior Customer Support Agents at Smarkets. I have completed an independent review of your complaint regarding unauthorised access to your account on 7 July 2026 and the loss of £142.73.

I understand your position that you did not authorise the activity, that you have never shared your password and have no connection to the Netherlands, and that the £142.73 should be refunded. Having carefully reviewed the account, I can confirm that our position remains unchanged.

On 7 July 2026 at 19:18 you received notification of an attempted sign in from the Netherlands. A new payment method was then added to your account and a £10 deposit was made from it. Your prior balance of £142.73 was reduced to £0 through bets placed while logged in with valid credentials. That attempted sign in was not a successful breach, and it does not alter the settlement of those bets.

The applicable Smarkets Terms and Conditions state:

Rule 2.14
"You must keep your login credentials secret at all times, and you remain solely responsible for the security and confidentiality of your account."

Rule 2.16
"If a bet is placed using your account, the bet will be considered to have been made by you, and therefore, once accepted by us, it shall be considered valid unless it contravenes any other term."

The bets were placed while logged in with your credentials and were accepted at the time, so under Rule 2.16 they are treated as having been placed by you and stand as valid. This is the position our support team previously provided, and it is correct.

You asked whether we can investigate the IP address and whether the new payment method was added by you. We have a record of the notifications you described, including the attempted sign in from the Netherlands, and of the new card being added and used for the £10 deposit. That card has now been removed and blacklisted so it cannot be used again. The location of an attempted sign in does not change how Rules 2.14 and 2.16 apply, because those rules turn on whether the correct credentials were used.

We have taken the security steps available to us: we froze the account on your report, removed and blacklisted the new card, and required ID verification before restoring access. You have since enabled two-factor login, which reduces the risk of further unauthorised access. We cannot trace funds beyond the platform or pursue a third party externally. [PLACEHOLDER FOR MICHAEL: if confirmed, add the external reporting route for the criminal matter. Do not name any agency unless confirmed.]

In summary, the account was correctly secured and the bets were settled in accordance with the Smarkets Terms and Conditions. Rules 2.14 and 2.16 do not provide for a refund in these circumstances. We are therefore not able to refund the £142.73.

This email constitutes Smarkets' final response to your complaint, and our position on this matter is final.

I have considered each of these points alongside your questions about the IP address, the new payment method, the tracing of the funds and the security steps we took.

Having carefully reviewed the account and all correspondence, I can confirm that our position remains unchanged.

On 7 July 2026 at 19:18 you received notification of an attempted sign in from the Netherlands. The notification was for an attempted sign in only. An attempted sign in does not establish that a successful breach occurred, and it does not change how your account was settled. Following that notification, a new payment method was added to your account and a £10 deposit was made from it. Your prior balance of £142.73 was then reduced to £0 through bets placed while logged in with valid credentials.

For clarity, the applicable Smarkets Terms and Conditions state the following:

Rule 2.14
"You must keep your login credentials secret at all times, and you remain solely responsible for the security and confidentiality of your account."

Rule 2.16
"If a bet is placed using your account, the bet will be considered to have been made by you, and therefore, once accepted by us, it shall be considered valid unless it contravenes any other term."

Rule 2.14 places responsibility for the security of your login credentials with you. Rule 2.16 provides that a bet placed using your account is considered to have been made by you and is valid once accepted. The bets that reduced your balance were placed while logged in with your login credentials and were accepted at the time. Under Rule 2.16 they are therefore treated as having been placed by you and stand as valid. Those rules turn on whether the correct credentials were used, not on where the sign in originated, so the location of the attempted sign in does not change their application. This reflects the position previously provided by our support team, which I have reviewed and confirm is correct.

You asked whether we can investigate the IP address and whether the new payment method was added by you. I have reviewed this. We have a record of the notifications you described, including the attempted sign in from the Netherlands on 7 July at 19:18. We can also see that a new payment method was subsequently added to your account and that a £10 deposit was made from it. As you noted, that card has now been removed and blacklisted so it cannot be used again. [PLACEHOLDER FOR MICHAEL: the depth of the IP and device review is not verified. You also asked why Smarkets does not pursue the person who obtained your password, and where the funds went. We have taken the steps available to us on the platform. Upon your report we froze your account, removed the new payment method and blacklisted it so it cannot be used again on Smarkets, and required ID verification before restoring access. You have now also enabled two-factor login, which is the right step to reduce the risk of further unauthorised access. We do not have the ability to trace funds beyond the platform, and we cannot pursue a third party who may have obtained your credentials outside it. We also cannot reverse settled bets that were valid under the Terms. [PLACEHOLDER FOR MICHAEL: the external reporting route for the criminal matter is not confirmed. We are not disputing what you have told us. The conclusions in this letter do not turn on where the sign in originated or on any disagreement about your account activity. They turn on the terms that govern the account: bets placed using the account with valid credentials are treated as placed by you and stand once accepted, and you remain solely responsible for the security of your credentials. On that basis we have not found grounds to depart from the Terms or to refund the balance.

In summary, we are satisfied that your account was correctly secured after your report, and that the bets which reduced your balance of £142.73 to £0 were settled correctly and in accordance with the Smarkets Terms and Conditions. Rules 2.14 and 2.16 apply whenever valid login credentials are used and do not provide for a refund in these circumstances. We are therefore not able to refund the £142.73.
